name: Scout player kit: third-person controller, weapon swap, dodge, crouch
player_behavior: The player controls a single goblin Scout in third person, live-swapping between daggers and bow, committing to weighty attacks, dodge-rolling with a brief invulnerability window, and crouching into a slow stealth stance.
acceptance_signals: A player character class with movement/camera setup and WASD + mouse-look input bindings
A weapon component or state owning dagger/bow live swap with per-weapon attack behavior
A dodge-roll ability with a ~0.22s invulnerability window and punishable recovery frames
A crouch stance that modifies movement speed and feeds the detection system
Combat hit resolution with hitstop, knockback and telegraphed wind-ups plus ground decals
Data-driven stat block for HP 110 / fast speed (single class this slice)

name: Hold-E interact channel framework
player_behavior: The player holds E to run interruptible channels — looting, taking down, binding, fouling the well, carrying, planting the Warren — with a progress read that cancels if interrupted.
acceptance_signals: A shared interaction component/interface driving timed, interruptible hold-to-complete channels
Interactable actors registering channel type, duration and completion effect
Cancellation on damage, movement or release, with progress feedback to HUD
Multiple consumers riding the same framework: loot, takedown, bind, foul well, carry, dig Warren

name: Torch toss, fire propagation, and the three burn objectives
player_behavior: The player throws a torch (Q) that sticks, ignites and spreads; the granary blazes compactly, a wheat field spreads row to row, and the windmill needs an aimed torch through a window for a two-stage detonation.
acceptance_signals: A projectile torch that attaches on impact and seeds an ignition source
A fire propagation system spreading between flammable actors/crop cells with per-type burn profiles
Burn-objective actors tracking burn state and completion, reporting to the raid objective tracker
Windmill objective with distinct Stage 1 Ablaze / Stage 2 Detonation states, window-hit detection, and a state-swapped smashed mesh
Fire registering as a town-wide noise/alarm signal and applying friendly-fire damage to any actor

name: Raid objective tracking, 30-minute clock and portal collapse
player_behavior: The HUD names the three objectives and shows an always-on 30-minute clock; Overlord whispers check in at 10 minutes, name a direction at 5, and point outright in the final 2; burning the last objective flares the stones open, then a 90-second collapse window ends the raid.
acceptance_signals: A raid-loop subsystem owning the countdown, timed whisper beats and end-of-raid transitions
Objective registry tracking the three assigned targets and their burned state, surfaced to HUD
Portal state machine: closed → open on final objective → collapse window with screen warning and stone-glow decay
Loss conditions on lives exhausted or player outside the circle at collapse end

name: Four-phase alarm escalation with soft signals
player_behavior: The hamlet visibly moves QUIET → SUSPICIOUS → RAID → RAZED; one soft signal (a confirmed sighting, a corpse, squawking flock, a distant patrol horn, an overdue patrol, or too many missing civilians) makes guards investigate and decays back to quiet, while a second signal, the bell, combat or fire escalates straight to RAID.
acceptance_signals: A town/alarm subsystem owning the current phase and never de-escalating past RAID
A soft-signal queue with source tagging, a decay timer back to QUIET, and instant escalation on a second signal
Signal emitters for sighting confirmation, corpse discovery, startled livestock, patrol horn, overdue patrol check-in, and civilian-absence census
Phase-driven changes to NPC behavior (investigate, watchman alertness, routines) with no HUD timers
RAZED phase silencing internal spawners and converging survivors

name: War-horn summoning and horde goblin pool
player_behavior: Pressing G blows the war-horn and 3–4 AI goblins sprint in from the treeline, up to 10 active, drawn from a finite raid pool of 20; dead horde goblins are gone for good and the treeline eventually goes silent.
acceptance_signals: A horde subsystem owning the 20-goblin reserve pool, active cap of 10, and per-blast summon count
Spawn logic that places goblins at treeline entry points and has them run in rather than appear
Pool accounting: permanent removal on death, return to reserve on courier delivery or Warren digging cost
Horn ability emitting a loud noise signal and marking the end of the quiet phase
Horde AI taking friendly fire like any other actor

name: Horde control: follow, frenzy, and the point context command
player_behavior: The horde loosely follows the player and auto-swarms anything that fights the player; aiming and pointing issues one context command — attack an enemy, smash a prop, or shoulder a loot sack, pig, or prisoner chain and courier it home.
acceptance_signals: A horde AI controller with Follow and Frenzy behavior states and threat propagation from player combat
A single point command that resolves target type under the aim reticle into attack / destroy / courier orders
Courier behavior state that navigates to the runic site or Warren, banks cargo, and returns the goblin to the summonable pool
Prisoner-escort variant with a capacity limit of three captives per goblin
Cargo drop on courier death at the death location

name: Crouch-and-confirm detection model
player_behavior: Guards must hold a sighting for about 1.5 seconds to confirm the player; breaking line of sight before that costs nothing, and a confirm produces exactly one soft signal that moves the town to Suspicious.
acceptance_signals: A perception component accumulating per-observer sight confirmation timers with reset on lost line of sight
Detection ranges modified by crouch stance and cover geometry
Watchman vision cone that visibly droops on a doze timer
Confirmation event emitting a single soft signal into the alarm subsystem
Tracking of whether any confirm occurred before the first fire, for the First Spark Unseen bonus

name: Noise events and guard investigation
player_behavior: Walking is quiet, running louder, smashing stalls and fences loud, and fire announces itself town-wide; guards move to investigate noises and startled chickens raise their own alarm.
acceptance_signals: A noise-emission API with per-action audible radii consumed by NPC hearing
Guard investigate behavior driving movement to the last noise location
Loud actions (smashing, digging the Warren, horn, fire) registering as signals to the alarm system
Startled-livestock noise events pulling the nearest guard

name: Takedown finisher and civilian bind
player_behavior: Approaching an unaware human from behind and holding E plays a silent committed finisher; on an unarmed civilian the same approach offers a longer, more interruptible bind that starts a rope chain instead of a body.
acceptance_signals: A takedown interaction requiring rear approach and target unaware state, with a committed interruptible animation
A separate bind channel available only on unarmed civilians, longer and more interruptible, producing a bound-captive actor
Rope-chain linking of bound captives behind their captor with self-escort movement penalty and no-attack restriction
Corpse actors that guards can discover, raising Suspicious on sight
Score hooks for takedown bonus, civilian captured, and watchman silenced by any silent method

name: Coin toss and greed AI
player_behavior: The player throws looted coins to make greedy humans — guards included — break off their post and scramble for the money.
acceptance_signals: A throwable coin actor consuming pouch currency and creating a greed lure
A greed stat on human AI that gates lure response priority over current task
AI state that abandons post/behavior to move to and collect the coin, then resumes
Lure interaction with the watchman-silenced score condition

name: Guards, patrols, watchtower bell, barracks and the finite raid-response pool
player_behavior: Four posted guards, a napping watchtower archer with a bell, forest patrols with a signal horn on a 5–7 minute sweep, a barracks spawning militia then archers then knights, and reinforcement squads marching from the castle — all drawn from one finite pool of 15 that can be emptied.
acceptance_signals: A defender-spawn subsystem owning a shared raid-response pool of 15 with tier/race-configurable size
Barracks spawner and map-edge reinforcement spawner both drawing from that single pool and falling silent when empty
Patrol AI on a 5–7 minute cadence with waypoint check-in tracking and an overdue grace timer that files a soft signal
Archer signal-horn ability with a committed interruptible wind-up triggered when the patrol is losing, escalating the town if completed
Watchtower bell interaction that escalates to RAID, plus a doze schedule
Destructible barracks and fouled-well interactions that permanently disable reinforcements and the bucket brigade
Data-driven enemy types (militia, archer, knight) with telegraphed attacks and score values

name: Loot, livestock carrying, and permanent banking at the stones or Warren
player_behavior: The player smashes strongboxes and stalls, gathers coins into a pouch with a hold-E channel, slings a squirming pig (or two chickens) over the shoulder, and banks loot permanently the instant it reaches the runic site or a planted Warren; dying spills the pouch as a lootable sack.
acceptance_signals: Separate accounting of provisional deeds versus physical loot, with loot banking permanently on delivery
Destructible container/prop actors gating a hold-E gather channel that fills a player pouch
A carry component with slow/no-fight restrictions, single large-item carry and dual chicken carry
Livestock actors with flee/catch behavior, kill-vs-steal score paths, and valid courier-target tagging
Pouch spill into a lootable sack actor on player death
Portal and Warren both acting as banking volumes for loot and prisoner chains
A Warren actor planted via loud hold-E channel, costing one horde goblin, limited to one active, destructible by guards, and serving as respawn point

name: Scoring, lives, and the end-of-raid judgement screen
player_behavior: Kills, arson, loot and mischief bonuses tally up; a successful exit multiplies deeds ×1.5 and adds +20 per unused life, and the end screen shows an itemized deeds/loot split, a letter grade, an Overlord verdict, and the player's personal best.
acceptance_signals: A score subsystem with a data-driven table of scoring entries and point values for objectives, loot, kills and bonuses
Bonus condition evaluators for First Spark Unseen, None Left Behind, watchman silenced, well fouled, barracks demolished and clean patrol wipe
Lives counter of 5 with respawn at the runic site or Warren, and unbanked-deed retention of 25% on failure
End-screen UI presenting itemized deeds/loot, letter grade, Overlord verdict line and persisted personal best
Verdict selection that varies flavor for prisoner-heavy raids

name: First-encounter tutorial prompts and Overlord barks
player_behavior: The first time the player meets each objective or mechanic, His Eternal Darkness delivers a bark plus a dismissible one-line HUD note naming the objective, payoff, and the one control that does it; a single settings toggle skips all of them.
acceptance_signals: A prompt subsystem tracking first-encounter flags per mechanic and firing bark + HUD note once
A data-driven bark/prompt table keyed to triggers (granary, field, windmill stage 1, patrol, civilian takedown/bind, livestock pen, courier)
A settings toggle that suppresses all prompts without gating any mechanic
Ambient bark playback for villagers and Overlord whispers on timed raid beats

name: Hand-authored tutorial hamlet, forest ring and runic site
player_behavior: The player crosses an authored forest with worn paths, roads, and signposts toward a fixed hamlet built from core-village, farmstead and windmill modules, with cover guaranteed between the treeline and every objective, and returns to the runic site to extract.
acceptance_signals: Authored level composed from reusable module prefab kits (core village, farmstead, windmill) with placed guards, patrols, civilians and livestock
A runic-site actor serving as spawn, respawn and extraction volume with open/closed visual states
Cover props (hedgerows, haycarts, fences, pen walls) registered for the stealth layer's sightline breaking
Wayfinding affordances: converging roads, signposts, landmark silhouettes visible from the forest, audible pens
Exactly one granary, one field and one windmill objective placed in a fixed layout

name: Civilians: routines, panic, bucket lines and self-looting
player_behavior: 6–10 civilians run daily routines, double-take in disbelief at a goblin, panic, join bucket lines to fight fires, and — as a stretch behavior — loot their own market stalls and bolt for home, competing with the player for the hamlet's gold.
acceptance_signals: Civilian AI with routine schedules, 10 HP, no attack, and panic/flee states
Bucket-brigade behavior that reduces fire progress unless the well is fouled
A census of civilians dead, bound or missing feeding the alarm subsystem's absence soft signal
Optional self-looting behavior triggered at peak chaos that removes stall gold from the map
Disbelief/double-take reaction behavior tied to barks
